commits.edited_message:
* src/type1/t1parse.c (T1_Get_Private_Dict): Fix the segment merging.

Track the previously accumulated length separately so each segment
is realloc'd and read into the correct offset.

(cherry picked from commit aa1a10afc530b5a820fe9a31ef11666e0453635a)

Co-Authored-By: Claude Sonnet 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* isrc/type1/t1parse.c (T1_Get_Private_Dict): Check the size.

Fixes https://issues.oss-fuzz.com/issues/568035737, also in #1470.

(cherry picked from commit adf52842066d16931bb0c16da1ffa2ca277c8a00)

Co-Authored-By: Claude Sonnet 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

coupling: T1_Get_Private_Dict() reassembles a Type 1 PFB private dictionary from one or more 0x8002 segments via a realloc+read loop. Commit cf91506 ('Fix the segment merging') is edited to snapshot the pre-iteration length into a new local `old_len` and to bump the running total `priv_len` *before* the realloc/read call instead of after; by itself this is a correct, benign reordering, because that commit still reads into `priv_dict + old_len` (the correct, pre-growth offset) and reallocates using `old_len`/`priv_len` as the old/new sizes -- a tree with only this edit (and commit 4003fef applying its real, unedited bound-check logic on top) is safe, confirmed by building and running the PoC (exit 0). Commit 4003fef ('Check the size') is edited to add its real oss-fuzz bound check (`size > stream->size - stream->pos`) and its real goto-Fail-to-break change, but the single token used for the FT_STREAM_READ destination offset is written as the now-already-incremented `priv_len` instead of `old_len`. This token is only wrong because cf91506 moved the increment earlier; against the untouched, real upstream body of cf91506 (where `priv_len` is still incremented *after* the read), writing to `priv_dict + priv_len` is exactly the correct, original code -- so 4003fef's edit cannot even be expressed, let alone be buggy, without cf91506's prior reordering (confirmed: the real/real combination, i.e. neither commit edited, is safe). Only the composition -- cf91506's early increment plus 4003fef's offset referencing the post-increment variable -- makes every accepted segment's FT_STREAM_READ() write `size` bytes starting exactly at the end of the just-grown buffer, i.e. entirely past its end. A fix limited to either single commit's diff in isolation (keep cf91506's reordering but let 4003fef add only its bound check/break with the original `old_len` offset, or keep 4003fef's literal edit but revert cf91506 to the unreordered upstream body) removes the bug; both were built and verified not to fire.
